newsitem.title: FRANCE: Daewoo still keen on Thomson Multimedia - paper.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo still keen on Thomson Multimedia - paper.

text.p: Daewoo Electronics Co chairman Soonhoon Bae said in a newspaper interview published on Friday he could still be interested in bidding for Thomson Multimedia (TMM) but said it would depend on how it is sold.

"It will depend on the privatisation method. If the matter is settled by private placement, I will have to look closely at the book of terms and conditions. Who knows, it might state that one must be French in order to qualify," he told business daily La Tribune.
"Last time the procedure was suspended because we are a foreign company," he added.

France called off a plan to sell the Thomson SA group, which owns defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF and television manufacturer Thomson Multimedia, last year after the Privatisation Commission objected.

The government had previously expressed a preference for selling Thomson SA to Lagardere, which had planned to sell on Thomson Multimedia (TMM) to Daewoo. The Commission objected mainly to the terms of the sale of TMM.
The government since decided to sell Thomson-CSF alone, and announced this week it would do so by private placement.
Soonhoon Bae also said the rest of the television industry was undergoing restructuring while TMM's financial situation had worsened over the last six months.
"Doubts about its privatisation have not helped it," he said.
